what: aide-memory npm publish is scoped via package.aide-memory.json (NOT root package.json). Its `files` field includes only: dist/memory/*.js, dist/cli/aide-memory.js, dist/cli/commands/memory/, scripts/hooks/, src/templates/rules/, README, LICENSE. Its `dependencies` are only 4: better-sqlite3, commander, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, zod. The root package.json (name: aide-v0) still lists old AIDE deps (tree-sitter-javascript, tree-sitter-typescript, ts-morph, chokidar, marked, marked-terminal, express, ws, axios, web-tree-sitter) and bins (aide-legacy: dist/cli/index.js) — those are dev-only and NOT what ships. scripts/build.sh does the publish build (tsc + copy templates + copy hooks). Binary migration target must match package.aide-memory.json scope, NOT the root package.json scope.
why: Critical scoping fact for the binary migration — elevated to always-inject per user. The plan and my earlier concerns conflated the dev monorepo's full codebase with what actually ships as aide-memory. Real scope: 4 deps, memory module + aide-memory CLI + memory CLI commands only. Every binary-migration phase spawn must see this immediately at session start.
